# Congestion and Curtailment Reductions
# Cost savings from reduced transmission congestion and renewable energy curtailment

greenfield_congestion_curtailment_reductions:
  congestion:
    constraints:

      flow_factor: 0.6 # flow factor is deliverability to the targeted constrained [0,1]
      # delta C_eff = S * capacity
      binding_hours: 1000 # binding hours is the number of hours per year that the line is binding (>= 0)
      average_exceedance: 560 # MW exceedance during binding hours (>= 0)
      # baseline congestion energy = H_b * X mwh/yr
      near_binding_hours: 0 # near binding hours is the number of hours per year that the line is near binding (>= 0)
      near_average_exceedance: 0 # MW exceedance during near binding hours (>= 0)
      # near baseline congestion energy = H_n * X mwh/yr
      near_binding_relief_factor: 0.25 # [0,1]
      saturation_factor: 0.3 # [0, something greater than 0??] (>= 0) # bascially 0 fora radial line and more for a meshed system

    costs:
      average_congestion_price: 30 # $/mwh (>= 0)
      residual_exceedance_value: null # $/MWh for residual exceedance (null = use average_congestion_price)
      value_of_lost_load: 0 # $/mwh (>= 0) # I alredady have this in the outages section will need to think about it (can tie a decrease
      # in congestion and curtailment to a decrease in outage risk and that has some value), but value of lost load should just live on the outage page, the methodology will reference it.

  curtailment:
    # Number of hours per year when renewable energy curtailment occurs
    # Curtailment happens when renewable generators must reduce output because
    # transmission capacity is insufficient to deliver power to demand centers
    curtailment_hours_total: 1000 # hrs/yr (>= 0) (set 0 if not applicable)

    # Average MW of renewable energy that is curtailed during curtailment hours
    # Total curtailed energy = curtailment_hours_total × average_curtailment_mw (MWh/yr)
    # The new line can relieve up to min(effective_capacity_relief, average_curtailment_mw) MW
    # Example: 300 hrs/yr × 250 MW = 75,000 MWh/yr potential curtailment relief

    average_curtailment_price: 30 # $/MWh (>= 0) (PPA proxy / avoided cost)

# Cost Incurrence Timing for AFUDC Capitalization
# Defines when costs hit CWIP (Account 107) during project lifecycle
# Per FERC USoA: AFUDC applies when (i) capex incurred AND (ii) activities in progress

cost_timing_patterns:
  # Build costs (conductor, structure, converter)
  build_costs:
    during_delay: 0.0 # % of cost incurred during delay (typically 0)
    during_construction: 1.0 # % spread uniformly over construction period
    afudc_eligible: true # Qualifies for AFUDC (in CWIP Account 107)

  # ROW acquisition costs
  row_acquisition:
    during_delay: 0.80 # Acquisition typically happens before construction
    during_construction: 0.20 # Final acquisitions during early construction
    afudc_eligible: true # Capitalized to plant cost

  # ROW holding costs (annual cost during delay)
  row_holding:
    during_delay: 1.0 # Holding costs occur only during delay period
    during_construction: 0.0 # No holding costs once construction starts
    afudc_eligible: false # Operating expense, not capitalized to CWIP

  # ROW rent costs (annual cost during operation)
  row_rent:
    during_delay: 0.0 # No rent during delay
    during_construction: 0.0 # No rent during construction
    afudc_eligible: false # Operational expense, not in CWIP

  # Environmental mitigation - base restoration
  environmental_mitigation_base:
    during_delay: 0.0 # Restoration happens during construction
    during_construction: 1.0 # Spread over construction period
    afudc_eligible: true # Necessary for plant to be ready for service

  # Environmental mitigation - credit purchases
  environmental_mitigation_credits:
    during_delay: 0.20 # Some credits purchased upfront (early permitting)
    during_construction: 0.80 # Most credits purchased as construction progresses
    afudc_eligible: true # Required for regulatory approval

  # Delay costs (regulatory/legal expenses)
  delay_costs:
    during_delay: 1.0 # By definition, occur during delay period
    during_construction: 0.0
    afudc_eligible: false # Typically expensed, not capitalized

  # O&M costs (operational period)
  operations_and_maintenance:
    during_delay: 0.0
    during_construction: 0.0 # O&M begins after COD
    afudc_eligible: false # Operating expenses

  # Insurance during construction
  construction_insurance: # THIS isnt not implemented yet but could be if I want to
    during_delay: 0.0
    during_construction: 1.0 # Spread over construction period
    afudc_eligible: true # Part of construction cost (can be capitalized)

# ============================================================================
# Primary BCR Configuration
# ============================================================================
#
# PURPOSE:
# This file controls which cost and benefit modules are included in the
# Primary BCR calculation. The Primary BCR is a customizable benefit-cost
# ratio that allows you to selectively include/exclude modules based on your
# analysis needs.
#
# HOW IT WORKS:
# - Setting a module to 'false' excludes it from the Primary BCR calculation
# - Setting a module to 'true' includes it in the Primary BCR calculation
# - If this file doesn't exist, all modules default to enabled
#   (Primary BCR = Capital+Delay BCR)
# - YAML configuration overrides command-line flags (--no_* flags)
#
# PRIMARY BCR FORMULA:
#   Primary BCR = (Included Benefits) / (Included Costs)
#
#   Included Benefits = Revenue (always) + checked benefit modules
#   Included Costs = Capital (always) + Delay (always) + checked cost modules
#
# ============================================================================
# COMMON BCR CONFIGURATIONS
# ============================================================================
#
# 1. CAPITAL+DELAY BCR (Default):
#    - All modules: true
#    - This is the default Primary BCR when no customization is done
#    - Formula: All Benefits / (Capital Costs + Delay Costs)
#
# 2. SYSTEM BCR (All-inclusive):
#    - All modules: true
#    - Note: System BCR is always calculated separately and includes everything
#    - Primary BCR matches System BCR when all modules are enabled
#
# 3. CAPITAL-ONLY BCR:
#    - All modules: false
#    - Only capital costs included (build, ROW, environmental)
#    - Formula: All Benefits / Capital Costs
#
# 4. EXCLUDE RISK COSTS:
#    - risk.wildfire: false
#    - risk.outages: false
#    - All others: true
#    - Formula: All Benefits / (All Costs - Risk Costs)
#
# 5. EXCLUDE EMISSIONS:
#    - energy.emissions: false
#    - All others: true
#    - Formula: All Benefits / (All Costs - Emissions)
#
# 6. EXCLUDE OPERATIONAL COSTS:
#    - operational.oandm: false
#    - operational.insurance: false
#    - All others: true
#    - Formula: All Benefits / (Capital + Delay + Risk + Energy)
#
# ============================================================================
# MODULE DESCRIPTIONS
# ============================================================================
#
# OPERATIONAL COSTS:
#   - oandm: Operations and maintenance costs (vegetation management, etc.)
#   - insurance: General operational insurance (conductors, structures, converters)
#   - delay_costs: Construction delay costs (legal, admin, regulatory, etc.)
#     NOTE: Delay costs are ALWAYS included in Primary BCR if calculated,
#           even if set to false here (the flag controls calculation, not inclusion)
#
# RISK COSTS:
#   - wildfire: Expected wildfire costs + wildfire liability insurance
#   - outages: Expected outage costs based on reliability parameters
#
# ENERGY COSTS:
#   - line_losses: Economic cost of energy losses (I²R and converter losses)
#   - emissions: Carbon and other emissions costs from line losses
#
# BENEFITS:
#   - congestion: Benefits from reduced transmission congestion
#   - curtailment: Benefits from reduced renewable energy curtailment
#   - revenue: Rate-based revenue requirement (ALWAYS included, not configurable)
#
# ALWAYS INCLUDED (Not configurable):
#   - Capital Costs: Build, ROW, Environmental Mitigation
#   - Delay Costs: Always included in Primary BCR if calculated
#   - Revenue: Rate-based revenue requirement
#
# ============================================================================
# CONFIGURATION
# ============================================================================

primary_bcr_config:
  # Operational costs that can be included/excluded from Primary BCR
  operational:
    oandm: true # Operations and maintenance costs
    insurance: true # General operational insurance
    delay_costs: true # Delay costs (always in Primary BCR if calculated)

  # Risk costs that can be included/excluded from Primary BCR
  risk:
    wildfire: true # Wildfire expected costs + liability insurance
    outages: true # Outage expected costs

  # Energy-related costs that can be included/excluded from Primary BCR
  energy:
    line_losses: true # Economic cost of energy losses
    emissions: true # Emissions costs from line losses

  # Benefits that can be included/excluded from Primary BCR
  benefits:
    congestion: true # Congestion reduction benefits
    curtailment: true # Curtailment reduction benefits
    # Note: Revenue is always included and not configurable here

17_congestion_curtailment_reductions.gre.description: We need the capacity from project technical details
delta C_eff = delta C_eff_new - delta C_eff_old
baseline congestion energy = H_b * X mwh/yr
near baseline congestion energy = H_n * X mwh/yr
transmission capacity is insufficient to deliver power to demand centers
THis is already expressed as "constraint-equivalent MW" conceptually

Higher values mean more saturation (less benefit per MW of capacity added)
